sources.title: SetWinEventHook
sources.documented_fact: Out-of-context notifications are queued in sequential order. The registering thread needs a message loop. Callback processing may reenter; successful registration returns a hook handle.
sources.engineering_inference: This is a delivery/registration contract, not an independently attested historical generation/coverage certificate.

sources.title: Guarding Against Reentrancy
sources.documented_fact: Additional events may reenter a callback; processing of a later event can finish first.
sources.engineering_inference: Distinguish guaranteed queue delivery order from application completion/journal order; unresolved reentrancy must halt.

sources.title: IsWindow
sources.documented_fact: The window can disappear after the check and recycled handles can identify a different window.
sources.engineering_inference: Matching handle values and endpoint existence do not establish a continuous window generation.

sources.title: EnumWindows
sources.documented_fact: Enumerates top-level windows, not general child windows; on Windows8+ this covers desktop-app top-level windows.
sources.engineering_inference: Enumeration yields a bounded current observation, not creation history or a full interval certificate.

sources.title: About Event Tracing
sources.documented_fact: ETW separates controllers, instrumented providers and consumers; enabled/disabled providers determine generation. Documented missing-event causes include size, buffers, consumers and disk throughput.
sources.engineering_inference: Transport statistics do not certify that an original target provider instrumented every required lifecycle transition.

sources.title: EVENT_TRACE_PROPERTIES
sources.documented_fact: EventsLost,LogBuffersLost,RealTimeBuffersLost describe session event/buffer recording and delivery loss.
sources.engineering_inference: Zero counters do not independently prove pre-subscription history or omitted/disabled source emission.

sources.title: EventWrite
sources.documented_fact: Routing depends on provider/event attributes. With no session recording the event, EventWrite does nothing and returns success.
sources.engineering_inference: A success code or signed zero-loss report alone cannot prove recording completeness.

sources.title: GetWindowThreadProcessId
sources.documented_fact: Retrieves the creating thread identifier and optionally its process identifier for a window.
sources.engineering_inference: PID/TID binding is useful but this API supplies no creation-anchored window generation token.

sources.title: GetProcessTimes
sources.documented_fact: Provides process creation/exit/kernel/user times; creation is a process FILETIME.
sources.engineering_inference: Bind PID to process creation time; do not treat it as the creation time of each of that process's windows.

sources.title: Event Constants
sources.documented_fact: CREATE/DESTROY events are documented for standard UI elements including window objects; accessible-object servers also generate these events. Parent destruction implies destroyed children.
sources.engineering_inference: Events are useful evidence;object/child identity and exact domain must be specified. This is not a claim that Windows emits no window events.

sources.title: CreateWindowExW
sources.documented_fact: A successful call returns a new HWND and sends creation messages before returning. Creation can fail.
sources.engineering_inference: A controlled owner could instrument every relevant creation path and failed/partial creation; no such cooperation exists for the original target here.

sources.title: WM_NCDESTROY
sources.documented_fact: DestroyWindow sends WM_NCDESTROY after WM_DESTROY and after child destruction; the owner receives it through WindowProc.
sources.engineering_inference: Owner messages can support an instrumented design, but the assessed message contract is not an independently complete crash/power-loss journal.

sources.title: PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutineEx
sources.documented_fact: Drivers register notifications for process creation and exit. Registration has integrity and lifecycle requirements.
sources.engineering_inference: Process notifications do not themselves attest every HWND lifecycle/generation; no driver is implemented or invoked.

sources.title: ObRegisterCallbacks
sources.documented_fact: Registers signed-kernel callbacks for process,thread and desktop handle operations.
sources.engineering_inference: This documented object domain is not a general full HWND lifecycle certificate. A signed binary alone does not prove its source coverage.

sources.title: Azure Attestation overview
sources.documented_fact: Attestation evaluates platform/TEE evidence under policies and returns cryptographic claims.
sources.engineering_inference: Platform/binary integrity claims need explicit event-source semantics to support lifecycle completeness;no service or real trust root is contacted.

sources.title: ProcessTrace
sources.documented_fact: ETW consumption attempts timestamp ordering,with documented ordering limitations for clock adjustments,equal-time events on different CPUs and invalid timestamps.
sources.engineering_inference: Timestamp presentation order is not an independent lossless causal/window-generation witness.

research_limit: Assessment of these documented mechanisms and supplied accepted source;not a universal Windows impossibility theorem. No concrete original-target provider/schema/attested complete interval source was identified.
unavailable_unused_reference: An earlier guessed SystemGuard runtime-attestation URL was inaccessible;not relied on. S15 is the retrieved primary attestation overview.
